introduction: This foundational level covers the basic physics of Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) and parameters governing wave motion (frequency, time period, wavelength). Strong baseline knowledge here is crucial for scoring direct points in formula-based NEET and JEE Main questions.

core_concepts.title: Condition for Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)
core_concepts.description: A periodic motion where the restoring force (or acceleration) is directly proportional to the displacement from the mean position and acts in the opposite direction: $F = -kx$ or acceleration $a = -\omega^2 x$.

core_concepts.title: Kinematic Equations of SHM
core_concepts.description: If motion starts from the mean position: Displacement $x = A \sin(\omega t)$, Velocity $v = A\omega \cos(\omega t) = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$, and Acceleration $a = -A\omega^2 \sin(\omega t) = -\omega^2 x$.

core_concepts.title: Time Period of a Simple Pendulum
core_concepts.description: For small angular displacements, the time period is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{l/g}$. Crucially, it is completely independent of the mass ($m$) of the bob.

core_concepts.title: Basic Wave Parameters
core_concepts.description: The fundamental relation connecting wave velocity ($v$), frequency ($f$), and wavelength ($\lambda$) is $v = f\lambda$. Wave velocity depends strictly on the medium's properties, while frequency is dictated entirely by the source.

important_entities.name: Phase ($\phi$)
important_entities.key_fact: Represents the state of motion (position and direction) at time $t$.
important_entities.significance: In the general equation $x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi_0)$, the term $(\omega t + \phi_0)$ is the total phase, and $\phi_0$ is the initial phase or epoch.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Maximum Velocity vs. Maximum Acceleration Positions
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Velocity is maximum at the mean position ($x = 0$, $v_{\text{max}} = A\omega$) where acceleration is zero. Conversely, acceleration is maximum at the extreme positions ($x = \pm A$, $a_{\text{max}} = \omega^2 A$) where velocity drops to zero. Do not mix up these boundary states.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: At half way out, KE is three-fourths
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: When the displacement is exactly half the amplitude ($x = A/2$), the Potential Energy (PE) is $25\%$ ($1/4$) of total energy, and the Kinetic Energy (KE) is $75\%$ ($3/4$) of total energy.

exam_strategy_tips: Remember that the total mechanical energy in SHM ($E = 0.5 m \omega^2 A^2$) remains strictly constant throughout the motion and is independent of time ($t$) or displacement ($x$).
